month_theme: Gap year decision week + Portugal prep

must_do.text: MONDAY JUNE 1 — Submit Duke Gap Year Program application. Deadline is today. Do not let this slip past midnight.
Duke housing and orientation — confirm registration status. Whether or not the gap year is approved, your enrollment needs to be in order.
Update your career plan — say 'update my plan'. It still references Northwestern. With Duke confirmed and the gap year pending, the plan needs a full revision before it can guide you accurately.

should_do.text: Portugal trip preparation — confirm all bookings (flights, accommodation, Sintra/Algarve day trips). Trip is in June.
Gap year activity planning — begin mapping phase 1 (Aug-Dec 2026): scuba certification registration in Coiba, glider project materials list, C++ course selection.
Begin C++ self-study — even one hour this week builds the habit. This is in the gap year plan and compounds over time.

could_do.text: Research Duke Pratt first-year ME course sequence and student aerospace project teams for when you arrive (Fall 2027 if gap year, Fall 2026 if not).
Draft intro email to 1-2 Duke ME/AE professors doing propulsion or dynamics research. No need to send yet — just draft it.

key_dates.event: Duke Gap Year Program application — DUE TODAY

notes: The gap year application is due Monday. Everything else this week is secondary to that. Once it is submitted, shift to two parallel tracks: Portugal trip preparation and gap year phase 1 planning. The career plan update is also important — the plan currently references Northwestern course numbers and project teams that do not exist at Duke. A revised plan is what keeps the monthly emails and weekly priorities calibrated correctly. Enjoy the Portugal trip — you earned it.
